correctness.rationale: A uniform-in-space marked Poisson construction is locally well-defined by bounded support and factorially summable time-ordered ancestor chains. Splitting proposals by head location relative to each vacant interval gives an internal no-proposal factor exp(-Lambda x), and two independent killed half-line survival factors. Connected deposited rods cannot influence the opposite half-line without first destroying interval survival; translation invariance equates the outer survival product to F=P(0,t). The stationarity mass-transport identity P(x)=integral (g-x)_+ q(dg) yields q=F Lambda^2 exp(-Lambda g) dg by two distributional derivatives. Direct deterministic-seed finite Monte Carlo with 35,196 and 20,637 gaps supports both heterogeneous tests. No finite computation substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The complete accessible 2007 head-exclusion article derives the same exponential profile only for a fixed rod length and symmetric orientations, and explicitly limits its exact closure to that setting. The new exact factorization is proved for independent positive bounded variable lengths, arbitrary time-dependent orientation marks and time-varying Poisson intensity, including distributions for which that particular empty-interval equation is not valid. The second directly relevant polydisperse article has different whole-rod-exclusion dynamics and does not imply the claim. Actual semantic published-finding corpus queries, locally accessible prior-claim searches, and targeted literature queries yielded no matching general theorem; this is originality relative to inspected evidence and is not exhaustive priority.

value.rationale: The full count-sampled gap-length law and count above every length threshold are natural damage/crack geometry observables; an exact universal exponential shape remains available even when random deposited sizes invalidate the monodisperse closed kinetics for overall coverage. This separates rate exposure from material size heterogeneity and allows inferential use of gap profiles. The theorem is a nontrivial exact robustness result, not a known-table recomputation or formal substitution, and it sharply distinguishes head-only adhesion from standard whole-rod exclusion.
